overview: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is Government of India's flagship initiative to create and promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship across the country. AIM's objective is to develop new programmes and policies for fostering innovation in different sectors of the economy, provide platforms and collaboration opportunities for different stakeholders, and create an umbrella structure to oversee the innovation & entrepreneurship ecosystem of the country. The Robotics & Automation scheme under AIM includes initiatives like Atal Tinkering Labs (ATL) which foster curiosity and innovation in young minds through 21st century tools and technologies such as robotics, IoT, 3D printing, and rapid prototyping tools.
objectives: Create and promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship across the length and breadth of the country
Develop new programmes and policies for fostering innovation in different sectors of the economy
Provide platforms and collaboration opportunities for different stakeholders
Create an umbrella structure to oversee the innovation & entrepreneurship ecosystem of the country
Foster curiosity, creativity, and imagination in young minds through 21st century tools and technologies
Inculcate skills such as design mindset, computational thinking, adaptive learning, physical computing etc.
Stimulate a problem-solving innovative mindset within children and nearby communities
Support dynamic entrepreneurs who want to build scalable and sustainable enterprises
eligibility: Eligibility varies by sub-programme: For Atal Tinkering Labs (ATL), schools across India can apply; for Atal Incubation Centres (AIC), universities, institutions and corporates can apply; for Atal Community Innovation Centres (ACIC), applicants must be from unserved/underserved regions with a partnership model requiring equal or greater matching funding; for Atal New India Challenge (ANIC), Indian companies incorporated under Companies Act 1956/2013, primarily MSMEs or DPIIT-recognized startups with majority stake held in India and a working prototype of the proposed solution relevant to the challenge area can apply.
benefits: Benefits include access to 21st century tools and technologies (IoT, 3D printing, robotics, rapid prototyping), mentorship through Mentors of Change program, funding support, technical facilities, resource-based support, partnerships and networking, co-working spaces, lab facilities, training programs, curriculum integration, evaluation and monitoring systems, and opportunities to participate in national innovation challenges and marathons. Financial support varies by programme: ATLs receive grant-in-aid for establishment, AICs receive support for operationalization, ACICs receive up to Rs 2.5 crores grant subject to matching funding, and ANIC provides funding up to INR 1 crore for selected startups.
financial_support: Financial support varies across AIM programmes: Atal Tinkering Labs (ATL) receive grant-in-aid for establishment with schools expected to set up ATL within 3 months of fund receipt; Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) receive support for operationalization including technical facilities and mentorship; Atal Community Innovation Centres (ACICs) receive a grant of up to Rs 2.5 crores subject to a partner proving equal or greater matching funding; Atal New India Challenge (ANIC) provides funding up to INR 1 crore to selected startups for prototype to commercialization over 12-18 months along with associated support from the AIM innovation ecosystem.
application_process: 1. Visit the official AIM website at aim.gov.in 2. Navigate to the specific programme section (e.g., ATL, AIC, ACIC, ANIC) 3. Check if the application portal is open (as noted on the homepage: 'Important Dear Applicants, please note that the application portal for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open') 4. If open, download guidelines and application forms from the respective programme page 5. Fill out the application with required details 6. Upload necessary documents 7. Submit the application through the designated portal 8. Await evaluation and selection as per the programme timeline 9. Upon selection, complete establishment or implementation as per guidelines 10. Submit utilization certificates and periodic reports via MyATL dashboard or equivalent systems.
required_documents: Monthly ATL activity report on MyATL Dashboard
Prototype or product details (for challenge-based programmes)
deadlines: Application portal for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open. Specific programmes like Youth Co:Lab have defined deadlines (e.g., Apply before midnight on 20th March 2026 for Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge 2026). ATL Marathon and School Innovation Marathon have annual cycles with announcements made via AIM website.
implementing_agency: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog, Government of India

caveats: Application portals for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open as per homepage notice
ACIC grant requires equal or greater matching funding from partner
ANIC supports startups only through prototype to commercialization stage (12-18 months)
Funds release for ATLs is contingent on performance and submission of Utilization Certificate
Programmes have specific eligibility criteria including age, incorporation status, and sector focus
GeM, PFMS and MyATL dashboard are mandatory for procurement, financial and operational updates respectively for ATLs
